news.title: The Diesel Crunch Isn’t Over Yet
news.summary: Oil prices have tumbled by more than 20% so far in November with Brent Crude sinking below $90 per barrel this week, as market participants and analysts bet on continued recovery of crude oil flows from the Strait of Hormuz. The oil market balance appears to be tipping into oversupply, forecasters say, and crude prices are reflecting this notion. But the product markets, especially the diesel market, remain tight, despite recent declines in diesel margins and retail prices. Retail diesel prices in the United States last week fell below $6 per gallon…

analysis.summary: Crude prices fell over 20% in November on Strait of Hormuz flow recovery and oversupply expectations, while diesel markets remain tight.
analysis.rationale: Expected Hormuz crude recovery and oversupply signal bearish crude pressure, offset by persistent tightness in refined diesel markets.

news.summary: The US Senate has launched an investigation into alleged ties between Vice President JD Vance and Vitol regarding an oil-trading contract for Venezuela. The report, dated November 11, quoted an unnamed source as saying JD Vance had met with a gasoline trader from Vitol named John Addison, whom Reuters described as “an old friend and early financier of his political career”…

analysis.rationale: The summary describes a political probe into past meetings and a trading contract without indicating any impact on Venezuelan crude supply or oil prices.

news.title: Washington Is Buying Its Way Out of China's Tungsten Grip
news.summary: Washington has signed tungsten deals worth up to $2.45 billion this year to build supply that does not depend on China, ahead of a Pentagon ban on Chinese-origin tungsten that takes effect on January 1. From that date, defense contractors can no longer deliver tungsten that was mined, refined, or separated in China, Russia, Iran, or North Korea, which closes the loophole that let them clear the old restrictions by finishing production elsewhere. The United States has not mined tungsten commercially since 2015. The government has signed a defense…

analysis.summary: The US signed $2.45B in tungsten deals ahead of a January 1 Pentagon ban on Chinese-origin tungsten.
analysis.rationale: The article focuses on defense critical mineral procurement and has no stated or direct implication for crude oil supply or demand.

news.title: Iraq Refuses to Accept OPEC+ Assessment of its Production Capacity
news.summary: Iraq is refusing to accept an OPEC+ assessment that says the country can sustainably produce less than 5 million barrels of oil per day. Baghdad wants OPEC+ to recognize a capacity of around 6 million bpd—an important acknowledgment ahead of the group’s upcoming Sunday meeting, at which production targets for 2027 are expected to be a topic of discussion. Under the current OPEC+ production agreement, Iraq's limit is 4.431 million bpd. If OPEC acknowledges the higher capacity assessment that Iraq is requesting, it would give Baghdad…

analysis.summary: Iraq rejected an OPEC+ capacity assessment below 5M bpd and is pushing for ~6M bpd recognition ahead of 2027 quota talks.
analysis.rationale: Iraq seeking higher recognized capacity to support larger future production quotas points to potential upward supply pressure within OPEC+.

news.title: Saudi Arabia Sees Smaller Economic Slump as More Oil Reaches Market
news.summary: Saudi Arabia now expects its economy to shrink 2.1% this year instead of 3.6%, after recovering enough oil exports to mitigate some of the damage caused by the Iran war. The revised forecast, announced in Tuesday's budget statement, is a considerable improvement from last month, but before the war began, Saudi Arabia had been expecting economic growth of approximately 4.5%. analysis.summary: Saudi Arabia improved its economic contraction forecast as October oil exports hit their highest level since the Iran war began via Yanbu.
analysis.rationale: Recovering Saudi crude export volumes through the East-West pipeline increase global oil supply availability, exerting downward price pressure.

news.title: Iran War Is Pushing Record Numbers of Fuel Tankers Into Crude Trade
news.summary: The Middle East crisis and upended crude and fuel flows have accelerated a shift in the global tanker fleet that began last year. A growing number of the so-called long-range-2 (LR2) clean tankers that have transported fuels such as diesel and gasoline have become the so-called dirty tankers and started shipping crude. As of this week, a record-high share of 75% of the global LR2 fleet is engaged in dirty crude transportation, while the number and share of tankers moving petroleum products, the so-called clean vessels, have dropped to record lows,…

analysis.summary: Middle East conflict is driving a record 75% of LR2 clean tankers into dirty crude shipping, leaving clean product tanker capacity at record lows.
analysis.rationale: Geopolitical conflict and disrupted flows are bullish for supply risk, while more tankers shifting into crude transport could ease crude shipping bottlenecks; the text does not directly quantify crude price impact.
